{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Kathleen Marie Madden''' is an American mathematician who works in [[dynamical system]]s. She was the dean of the School of Natural Sciences, Mathematics, and Engineering at [[California State University, Bakersfield]].  She won the [[George Pólya Award]] and is the co-author of the book ''Discovering Discrete Dynamical Systems''.

==Education and career==
Madden did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Colorado]].{{r|csub}} She then spent two years with the [[Peace Corps]] teaching mathematics in [[Cameroon]] before returning to the US for graduate study.{{r|polya}}
She completed her Ph.D. in 1994 at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]]; her dissertation, ''On the Existence and Consequences of Exotic Cocycles'', was supervised by Nelson G. Markley.{{r|mgp}}

Before joining California State University, Bakersfield as associate dean in 2015,{{r|csub}}
she was a faculty member in the mathematics department at [[Lafayette College]]{{r|polya}}
and then at [[Drew University]], where she also served as chair of the department and associate dean. At California State University, Bakersfield, she was appointed interim dean in 2016 and permanent dean in 2017.{{r|csub}}  She served in this position until 2021, at which time she retired to a part-time position in the faculty.{{r|csub2}}  

==Books and recognition==
In 1998, Madden and [[Aimee Johnson]] won the George Pólya Award for their joint paper on [[aperiodic tiling]], "Putting the Pieces Together: Understanding Robinson's Nonperiodic Tilings".{{r|polya}} In 2017, Madden, Johnson, and their co-author [[Ayşe Şahin]] published the textbook ''Discovering Discrete Dynamical Systems'' through the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|ddds}}
